text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Spanish media react angrily to finance minister Gerrit Zalm's statement that countries such as Spain, Italy and Portugal are not among leading qualifiers for EMU. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok, who now holds rotating EU presidency, wants results at the Amsterdam summit in June. (p1)
- Publisher VNU increases net profit and EPS in 1996 by around 15 pct. (p1)
- Food retailer Ahold reports higher sales of Dfl 36.5 bn in 1996. (p1)
- Vendex's bid for remaining shares in French temp agency Bis has a good chance of succeeding as the BIS share price dropped on Tuesday. (p1)
- Property fund Enhobel rejects rival Uni-Invest's public bid. (p3)
- German unit of steelmaker Hoogovens buys French aluminium panel producer Alfal from Pechiney. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Consumers have to pay more for cable TV subscription. (p1)
- Rise of house prices in the Netherlands expected to slow this year due to rising interest rates. (p2)
- ING bank applies for licence to operate in Ukraine. (p17)
- Insurer Stad Rotterdam sells its 5.2 percent stake in Kas-Associatie. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Philips gets major decoder order from Spain. (p1)
- Growing number of consumers and businesses in problems through rising heating costs due to cold weather. (p1)
- Schiphol Airport to invest 500 million guilders for modernisation. (p23)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier takes over small French legal and fiscal publisher La Documentation Organique. (p23)
TROUW
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend's attempts to lure back big concerns through changing the tax regime, appears to have been a success. (p6)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Central planning bureau CPB and Rotterdan Port authority GHR quarrel about starting point for expansion of port on the second Massvlakte. (p1)
- Public transport system experiments with smart payments card. (p1)
